[Skip to main content](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/webPUlth/shared-parental-leave-spl#main-content) # Shared Parental Leave (SPL) - SupportGoWhere Shared Parental Leave (SPL) Share link Support eligible working parents in sharing parental responsibility and caring for their infants. SCHEME HIGHLIGHTS - Government reimbursement/payment capped at $2,500 per week - Leave may be taken in one continuous block or non-continuously [Apply now](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/share-my-leave) Expand all sections About this support | | SPL (2013) | SPL (from 1 Apr 2025) | | **Amount of leave entitled** | Eligible working fathers can take up to 4 weeks of leave from their wife’s Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) or Adoption Leave (AL). | Child’s birth or estimated delivery date or Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date: 
- If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, up to 6 weeks of leave to be shared between parents 

- If on or after 1 Apr 2026, up to 10 weeks of leave to be shared between parents | | **Amount of government reimbursement/payment** | Government reimbursement/payment capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $10,000 for 4 weeks. | Government reimbursement/payment capped at $2,500 per week. | | **Flexibility of leave** | Flexibility for leave to be taken in one continuous block or non-continuously, with mutual agreement between employer and employee. | | **When can SPL be taken?** | Within 12 months from the child's date of birth. | - After Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML)/ Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL)/ Adoption Leave (AL) is fully consumed; and  

- Within 12 months from the child’s date of birth. | Who is this for? Parents whose child is born, or has an estimated delivery date (EDD), or formal intent to adopt (FIA) date **on or after 1 Apr 2025**, are entitled to the [new SPL scheme](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/shared-parental-leave) and should not be making an election for 2013-SPL. | | SPL (2013) (For father) | SPL (from 1 Apr 2025) (For both father and mother) | | **For live births** | - Your child is a Singapore citizen or becomes one within 12 months from birth  

- Child's birth or estimated delivery date is between 1 Jul 2017 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive) 

- Wife is eligible for Government-Paid Maternity Leave or Adoption Leave and agrees to share the leave 

- Married to child's mother between conception and birth or within 12 months from birth | - Your child is a Singapore citizen or becomes one within 12 months from birth  

- Child’s birth or estimated delivery date:

- If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, entitled to 6 weeks of SPL 

- If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks of SPL
-  For fathers: Lawfully married to the child’s mother between conception and birth or within 12 months from birth 

- For employee: Served employer for at least 3 months before child’s birth

- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before child’s birth | | **For stillbirths** | - The date of stillbirth is between 1 Nov 2021 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive) 

- Either you or the child’s mother are Singapore citizens | NIL | | **For adoptive child** | - Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date between 1 Jul 2017 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive) 

- Married to the adoptive mother when the election for 2013-SPL was made 

- If child is not Singapore citizen (SC), either you or the adoptive mother has been SC since the child’s dependant’s pass issuance | - Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date: 

- If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, entitled to 6 weeks of SPL 

- If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks of SPL
- Not the natural father or mother of child 

- If child is not Singapore citizen (SC), either adoptive mother or father of child has been SC since the child’s dependant’s pass issuance 

- For employee: Served employer for at least 3 months before FIA date 

- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before FIA date | How to apply? **For SPL (2013)** - Discuss and agree on the leave arrangement with your wife. - Your wife must declare her intention to share her leave through the [Share My Leave eService](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/share-my-leave) in the Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal no earlier than 16 weeks before your child’s estimated delivery date. | | | | --- | --- | | **For employees:** | Notify your employer of the leave arrangement and submit the [declaration form (SPL1)](https://go.gov.sg/spl1form) with necessary documents. | | **For self-employed:** | Record your SPL dates and submit your claim online via the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) within 3 months after the last date of your SPL. | | **For employers:** | - Obtain and verify the [declaration form (SPL1)](https://go.gov.sg/spl1form) and supporting documents from your employee. 

- Keep the declaration form or records for 5 years from the last leave date for audit purposes. 

- Verify that your employee’s wife has made a declaration to share her leave in the Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal. Check all supporting documents to confirm your employee’s eligibility. 

Submit your claim for reimbursement online via the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) no later than 3 months after the last date of your employee’s SPL. | **For SPL (from 1 Apr 2025)** Please refer to details on the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/shared-parental-leave/). Where can I find help? For SPL (from 1 Apr 2025), [view more details](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/shared-parental-leave). For the SPL (2013), [view more details](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/2013-shared-parental-leave) * * * MSFCares: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222) (say ‘GPLS’ when asked for the hotline you want to reach) Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore. * * * [Submit an enquiry](https://go.gov.sg/contact-gpls) Scheme last updated 01 Sep 2026 Try our AI search
